messages:
maria: FYI found multiple Go ecosystem advisories impacting us — grpc, golang.org/x/oauth2 (jwt handling), and a net/http header parsing issue. Collecting triage data now, need prioritization and patch plan.

aj: Can you link the advisories? I want to know the exploitability surface (public endpoints vs internal).

maria: Links: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-grpc-example (grpc advisory), https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/golang.org/x/oauth2 (oauth/jwt advisory), and a Go runtime fix note for net/http (requires Go 1.20.7+). All three are in our dependency graph; grpc is used by public inference API and several internal services.

samir: Quick read: grpc advisory looks high severity (deserialization/exec path in reflection?); oauth/jwt looks medium (token parsing edge case could allow bypass if we use unvalidated keys). net/http fix is low unless we expose raw headers to untrusted clients.

kevin: We should assume public-facing services (hosted API) are high risk. Dedicated and Private deployments are lower internal risk but we need patches for tenant isolation code. Suggest block: grpc -> immediate, oauth/jwt -> next sprint, net/http -> schedule with Go runtime bump.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Pin grpc to patched release in go.mod and cut emergency branch for hosted-api; 2) Add runtime request filtering for suspicious payloads; 3) Add additional audit logging for token validation failures (for the oauth/jwt case).

aj: For pinning, recommend a single-line replace so we don't get accidental transitive upgrades. Example we used before:
```
// in go.mod
replace google.golang.org/grpc => google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.0
// then in CI
go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.0
```
We'll also run `go list -m all | grep grpc` across services to verify.

maria: I've opened an emergency branch: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/tree/sec/grpc-patch and a Jira SEC-4823. I'll add the `go get` commands and a short e2e that hits the reflection code path.

samir: For oauth/jwt, can we add a token validation guard in the auth middleware as a short-term defense? If we canonicalize keys and reject unknown alg headers we reduce blast radius.

kevin: Yes, add strict alg whitelist + JWK key id checking. Also enable audit logs on validation failures and route logs to the security S3 bucket with retention for 90 days.

maria: Deploy-bot: start a canary deploy of the grpc-patch branch to staging and run smoke tests.

deploy-bot: @maria starting canary deploy to staging (canary-3 pods) for sec/grpc-patch. Will report status in ~12m.

aj: CI note — update our go-versions matrix: some internal services pin Go 1.19; net/http fix requires 1.20.7+, so we'll need a limited Go runtime upgrade plan. Keep that as a separate rollout ticket.

maria: Action items: (1) emergency grpc pin + canary (maria/aj) — SEC-4823; (2) oauth/jwt middleware hardening + audit logging (samir/kevin) — SEC-4824; (3) plan Go runtime bump for net/http fix (kevin) — SEC-4825. I'll update the triage doc and mark grpc as P0.

kevin: Sounds good. If canary passes we should prepare a customer-facing note for hosted API tenants about a quick maintenance window — low risk but transparent.

maria: I'll draft a short status post for #announcements and the incident page if anything changes. Thanks all.
